page: Vultr vcg-a40-4c-20g-8vram is a fractional GPU instance within the Cloud GPU family. It features 4 shared Intel x86_64 vCPUs with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 20.0 GB of system memory. The instance includes a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with a 0.1667 allocation providing 8 GB of dedicated VRAM, alongside 360 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in specific workloads, particularly LLM inference. For a small 135M model, prompt processing reaches 9881.81 tokens per second and text generation achieves 465.27 tokens per second, both placing in the top tier. Similarly, a medium 7B model yields top-tier results with 3161.22 tokens per second for prompt processing and 107.91 tokens per second for text generation. However, general compute and database performance show limitations. Passmark database operations and static web serving throughput are weak, scoring in the bottom 25 percent, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 10 percent.

This instance offers a cost-effective entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads by utilizing a fractional GPU and shared CPU allocation, avoiding the higher expenses of dedicated full-GPU hardware. It is highly suitable for small to medium LLM inference, lightweight machine learning development, and GPU-accelerated data processing. It is less suitable for high-throughput web serving, heavy multi-threaded CPU tasks, or intensive database operations due to its shared CPU architecture and lower multi-threaded performance.

Acceleration is provided by a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM. In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates top-tier performance for LLM inference, achieving 3161.22 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 7B model. However, its shared CPU architecture results in weaker performance for database operations and multi-threaded decompression. This instance is best suited for lightweight machine learning inference, model prototyping, and GPU-assisted development tasks where a full dedicated GPU is not resource-efficient.
